programs.name: Arizona Assurance
programs.description:
Arizona Assurance (AZA) is a grant program that was created to increase the number of college graduates from the state of Arizona who come from low-income households. AZA provides both financial aid and support services; these work together to retain and graduate students. This is achieved through first-year transition programming, mentoring, leadership building, career development, graduate/professional school preparation, and planning for life after college.

For more information on eligibility criteria, selection, and funding please visit: The Office of Scholarships & Financial Aid - Arizona Assurance Program

If you have any questions about AZA support and programming, email us at aza@arizona.edu or call the office at 520.626.3656.
programs.mentoring_information: All Arizona Assurance scholars participate in Thrive Peer Mentoring.
programs.eligibility: Students must be invited to apply before their first-year by the Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid.

programs.name: Associated Students of the University of Arizona - Near You
programs.description: The Associated Students of the University of Arizona Near You (ASUANY) works to enhance the quality of student life through academics, activities, community involvement, clubs and organizations, service, and advocating for online and location students. The Executive Board for this student government body represents the student voice in the discussions and decisions that shape all aspects of Wildcat life for location and online students, both academically and socially. The Associated Students of the University of Arizona Near You (ASUANY) exists to foster and enhance communications between the student body and the university community; to provide a forum for discussing and defining the role of students in the university; to represent and advocate their concerns within the university community and statewide; to serve as a resource for student inquiries and requests; to advise and make recommendations on existing and proposed University policies and procedures.
programs.eligibility: - A candidate for an executive office shall be an undergraduate student of the University of Arizona Online and Near You Network, with a minimum of six (6) units per semester, during the regular academic year of election and during the term of office.

programs.name: Biology Research Abroad: Vistas Open! (BRAVO!)
programs.description:
BRAVO! is a summer research program which funds proposals for UA undergraduates who have at least 6 months of research experience to conduct research abroad with an international collaborator of their current UA research mentor for 10-12 weeks during the summer. This experience serves to further ongoing collaboration between your mentor’s research group and their foreign colleague, promote progress on a specific project, and/or facilitate the exchange of best practices and techniques, while providing a unique opportunity for you to grow scientifically and culturally through immersion in the global scientific community.
 
If you didn’t think it possible to pursue an opportunity abroad due to limitations in funding or lack of experience in international travel, think again. BRAVO! provides full financial support up to $8,000 for the summer abroad, which typically covers all costs for airfare, lodging, food, passport and visa fees, research supplies, and other travel-related expenses. Students who are financially challenged (i.e. eligible for the Pell Grant or federal work-study) may also request a stipend. The BRAVO! Director will assist all BRAVO! participants in preparing for and navigating through their international experiences.
programs.eligibility:
Applicants must be UArizona undergraduates with an expected graduation date of December 2026 or later.
Applicants must have at least six months of research experience with their UArizona mentor at the time of application.
Applicants must be mature, responsible, independent, and would serve well as a representative of their mentor’s lab and of the University of Arizona.
Priority is for students with limited travel experience and/or limited ability to travel internationally without support (e.g. students who are financially challenged, first-generation, have never been outside the U.S., etc.)

programs.name: CALES Ambassadors
programs.description:
Are you passionate about your major? Do you enjoy meeting new people? Are you looking for a unique professional development opportunity? If so, apply to become a student Ambassador in the College of Agriculture, Life & Environmental Sciences (CALES)! As the face of the college, and often of the university, ambassadors volunteer their time to connect prospective students to academic opportunities in CALES and at the university.

The CALES Ambassador Program is a prestigious leadership program. Members develop an enhanced sense of professional self-efficacy through competency-based learning focused on leadership, presentation, interpersonal and organizational skills. While the application process is competitive, successful applicants will become student leaders in CALES, receive a 100% Engagement notation, and join the robust network of CALES Ambassador Alumni upon graduating.
programs.length: 1 year commitment but renewable each year
programs.eligibility: At least 1 semester in CALES; 3.0+ GPA

programs.name: EHS-RISE: Environmental Health Sciences - Research for Indigenous Student Engagement
programs.description: EHS-RISE is an introductory summer research program which aims to increase the representation of Native Americans in the STEM workforce, while supporting students’ cultural identity. The program is designed uniquely for Native American and Alaska Native freshmen, sophomores, and first-year transfer students majoring in STEM at UArizona who are seeking a summer research experience. EHS-RISE offers participants a full-time, paid 12-week research experience on a project related to environmental health sciences (environmental factors that impact human health) and provides housing, professional development workshops, and spiritual and community activities.  EHS-RISE is offered in conjunction with the Undergraduate Biology Research Program (UBRP).
programs.eligibility:
University of Arizona Native American and Alaska Native undergraduates who are graduating in December 2026 or later. Priority will be given to freshman and transfer students in their first year at UArizona, as well as those who do not have prior research experience, but all applicants will be considered. Students must be at least 16 years old by the time the summer program starts (May 18, 2026).
A degree-seeking student majoring in a science, technology, engineering, or math field, and has a suitable interest in obtaining research experience in environmental health sciences.
In good academic standing (holding an overall University of Arizona GPA of 2.0 or higher)
U.S. Citizens or permanent residents.

programs.name: New Start
programs.description:
Join the 50 year UA TraditionFor 50 years, the New Start Summer Program has been offering new Wildcats the opportunity to get a head start on their college degree while getting to know the UA campus and meeting new people. That's over 14,000 students! 
By participating in New Start, you will:
Earn 6-7 units of academic credit
Get connected with returning Wildcats who not long ago were in your shoes
Meet hundreds of other new UA students
You'll get connected with faculty, learn about what UA has to offer, get crucial advice from peer mentors and resident assistants, and academic support from tutors. By the time you complete New Start, you'll be a half a semester closer to your degree! You will feel like a UA expert ready for your first year, and will meet some of the best friends you'll ever have!

While that all sounds great, here are some numbers to convince you even more. New Start students continue into their sophomore year at a rate 6-10% higher than their peers who did not participate in New Start. Plus, New Start is very affordable, providing reduced tuition and fees for Arizona residents and covering all costs for Pell recipients through our Pell Promise.

And it doesn't stop after summer! With the support of the Thrive Center, New Start students now have the opportunity to get support and community throughout their entire fall semester with drop-in hours and planned social and educational events! Come, join the New Start family!
programs.mentoring_information: Every New Start participant is assigned a peer mentor.  This mentor meets with them at least three times individually throughout the program, and leads their peer mentoring group Monday through Thursday for HED 297A.
programs.eligibility:
You are eligible to attend the New Start Summer Program if you meet the following requirements:
You will graduate from an Arizona high school during the 2024-2025 academic year and you have not attended college. (If you're dually enrolled at a community college while you're in high school, you may still apply!)
You have been admitted to the University of Arizona and plan to enroll here in a degree-seeking program for Fall 2025.
You have completed and submitted all required New Start documentation by the required Dates & Deadlines. You must complete both the 2024–2025 and 2025-2026 FAFSA forms in order to receive financial aid for New Start.
In the meantime:
Apply for fall admission in a degree-seeking program!
Please prepare to file your 2025-2026 FAFSA. While you wait, start by learning and creating your FSA ID! You will need this to move forward with your FAFSA, and since there will be some processing time needed, it doesn't hurt to create this now.

programs.name: UA Hispanic Alumni Scholars
programs.description:
The University of Arizona Hispanic Alumni (UAHA) community is made up of accomplished Hispanic graduates and former students of UArizona who live throughout the world. UAHA was founded in 1982 to promote academic excellence among Hispanic students at the university, provide financial and mentoring support to qualified and deserving students, and develop links between alumni and supporters in the professional and business community. Since 1986, UAHA has awarded nearly 2,500 scholarships worth more than $5.3 million.

UA Hispanic Alumni Scholars are recipients of renewable scholarships from UAHA.  In addition to scholarship funds, recipients also receive direct support from Thrive Center and the Adalberto y Ana Guerrero Student Center.  UAHA scholars participate in Thrive Peer Mentoring their first two years and then are encouraged to pursue experiences that support their future integration into the workforce or graduate/professional school during the remaining two years.  Transfer scholars participate for two years, with the first year supporting by Thrive Peer Mentoring an the second focused on workforce/graduate school integration.
programs.length: 2 to 4 years, depending on the scholarship type
programs.mentoring_information: Each UAHA scholar is assigned a peer mentor.  Thrive peer mentors are paid, trained undergraduate students who provide one-on-one support to fellow undergraduates.  Peer mentors employ active listening strategies coupled with knowledge of campus resources and student success strategies to provide guidance, accountability and connections for their mentees.
programs.eligibility: Students must be recipients of a UA Hispanic Alumni scholarship to participate.  Students can apply on scholarship universe.

programs.name: Undergraduate Biology Research Program (UBRP)
programs.description: The Undergraduate Biology Research Program (UBRP) is an educational program designed to teach students science by involving them in biologically related research in the laboratory or field. Students are paid for conducting research in their full-time summer placements, where they develop an understanding of the scientific method, receive a realistic view of biological research, and are mentored by faculty. They also acquire the tools necessary to be successful in post-graduate studies in biology should they choose careers related to biology or research. Students begin UBRP with a full-time summer research apprenticeship, and then have the option to continue in UBRP on a part-time basis during the academic year, to accommodate classes.
programs.eligibility: UBRP is open to UA undergraduates from all majors, class standings, and career interests. See program website for specific eligibility criteria.
